paper.title: Caffeine improves working memory in adults

paper_text:
Caffeine improves working memory in adults
Brown, A., Kim, S.  J. Fake Neuroscience, 2019

Abstract
In a double-blind trial of 90 adults, 200 mg caffeine improved n-back accuracy by 12% compared with placebo.

Results
Figures 2 to 4 show accuracy by dose. The improvement was significant at 200 mg (p = 0.01).

alerts.description: A retraction notice was published for this paper.

notice.text:
Retraction: Caffeine improves working memory in adults

The journal has retracted this article. An institutional investigation found that the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated, and the conclusions cannot be relied on. The authors have not responded.

Caffeine and study performance

1. Introduction
Caffeine is widely used by students. Brown and Kim [3] showed that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why we chose a 200 mg dose for our experiment.

2. Methods
Participants received 200 mg caffeine or placebo.

References
[3] Brown, A., Kim, S. (2019). Caffeine improves working memory in adults. J. Fake Neuroscience.
